paragraphs: Four Texts, Four Readers, posted by Lily. At the school fair, we found four short texts. Leo and May collected the texts, and I wrote this post. Each text is for a different reader. I put each text in a separate paragraph, so it is easy to find. When you read a text, ask first, "Who is this for?" The first words often give you the answer. Can you find the readers?

Text One is a sign on the green table. It says, "Hello, children! Try a tasty fruit cup, and pay only ten baht." The reader is a child, because the sign says "children". The words are short and friendly. Children like short sentences and a happy picture. Leo drew a big smile on the sign.

Text Two is a note from Teacher Kim. It says, "Dear parents, please keep the receipt, because we need it at the gate." The reader is a parent, because the note starts with "Dear parents". The language is polite and clear. Parents read this note at home, so it must be clear. Every child takes the note home in a bag.

Text Three is a message to the teachers. It says, "Dear teachers, every class can rent one table for the fair." The price is twenty baht, except for the youngest class, because it rents a table for free. The reader is a teacher, because the message starts with "Dear teachers". This text is more formal than the sign. Teachers have little time, so the message is short.

Text Four is a notice on the web page of the fair. It says, "Dear customers, a ticket for a visitor costs thirty baht." The reader is a customer, because the notice starts with "Dear customers". The web page has a big title and a clear button. A customer wants facts, and the page gives the price at once. Leo made the page, and May checked the price.

Grace wrote in an email that a fruit cup at her school costs one dollar and fifty cents. A dollar has one hundred cents, so that is one hundred and fifty cents. Grace also asked what a fruit cup costs here, and I answered ten baht. The same fair has four different readers, and each text uses different words. Which text is for you? Tell us in a comment!
